findings.observed: AcceptanceBroker construction calls validate_seed_manifest and raises AdmissionError: seed hash mismatch: TARGET_CHARTER.md. The file SHA-256 is 43a43f2f6a494e1b5e9b2eb118e6a43765304d2630d379e607e56d4e725a3a63, while the manifest declares 5aea61dec6babcc2dd09abecc41349139f1e5fc01c2ec6f10df9af18beeb8a78.
findings.expected: The exact five-file seed validates before a broker can materialize a fresh disposable target repository.
findings.reproduction: From branch tip 2a451ff851bb78ced9c1461078d15e1641fac78c run: python -m unittest orchestrator_harness.tests.test_firmware_acceptance_target -v. The closed-contract test passes and both broker-materialization tests fail at validate_seed_manifest before Git initialization.
findings.impact: The public acceptance kit cannot materialize any target, so the target/evidence campaign and its hash-bound provenance cannot start.
findings.no_fix_consequence: C43 target creation and every dependent C49/C63/C65 acceptance proof remain blocked on every run.
findings.smallest_fix: Correct the TARGET_CHARTER.md hash in TARGET_SEED_MANIFEST.json to the accepted file bytes, or restore the charter bytes intended by the declared hash; add or retain the existing seed validator regression.
findings.complexity: One manifest-or-seed-byte correction plus the focused target test.
findings.regression_risk: Low and bounded to the sealed seed identity; the public validator immediately verifies the chosen canonical bytes.
findings.verification_cost: Rerun only orchestrator_harness.tests.test_firmware_acceptance_target after the accepted correction.
findings.alternatives: Bypassing, weakening, or deferring seed validation would violate the exact five-file hash-bound contract and has higher provenance risk.
findings.cost_benefit: A one-line identity correction restores the mandatory target-materialization entrypoint, while leaving it unresolved prevents all downstream acceptance work.
